title: Black Twitter Is Thriving—on Threads
gist: Wired argues Meta's Threads has become the spiritual successor to Black Twitter, drawing Black cultural voices who left X after Musk's takeover, while Bluesky/Blacksky stalled on scale; Threads' Instagram/Facebook onboarding and 500M+ MAU put it on track to pass X's 557M.

insights.claim: Threads has emerged as a vital artery of the Black social media ecosystem, at times rivaling the cultural influence Black Twitter once had, as shown by the outcry over the Nolan Wells grand jury decision.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Shift of an influential cultural community toward Meta strengthens Threads' engagement and ad-relevance versus X.
insights.quote: Threads is proving to be its spiritual successor

insights.claim: Prominent Black voices such as Roxane Gay, Brittany Packnett Cunningham and Nikole Hannah-Jones have migrated from X to Threads, pulling high-engagement discourse with them.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Creator migration is a leading indicator of platform share shifts in social media.
insights.locator: Today, some of the biggest cultural voices

insights.claim: Threads users are deliberately building a shared narrative of 'Threads history', mirroring how Black Twitter functioned as the center of a hypernarrative web.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Community identity formation signals durable network effects rather than transient usage.
insights.quote: People talk about events in Threads history like they did and do with Black Twitter
insights.locator: One of the most striking things

insights.claim: Black Threads is not an exact replica of Black Twitter: live-tweeting of award shows and sports events, where Black Twitter shined, has not yet materialized on Threads.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Real-time event engagement is a key monetizable gap Threads has not yet closed versus X.
insights.quote: Black Threads doesn’t feel like an exact replica of Black Twitter to me
insights.locator: Though many of the same people

insights.claim: Threads and TikTok users first raised awareness of a two-week blackout in majority-Black Gary, Indiana before national media covered it, showing the platform can move news agendas.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Agenda-setting power increases a platform's value for news distribution and advertisers.
insights.quote: Then news outlets started paying attention.
insights.locator: Even so, the platform has been able

insights.claim: Some Black users caution that Threads remains a platform owned by others, warning against getting too comfortable.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Platform-dependency risk can trigger another migration if Meta policy shifts.

themes.theme: X's decline after the Musk takeover

insights.claim: After Elon Musk bought Twitter in 2022 and renamed it X, day-one users found it less functional, hate speech and propaganda accounts surged, and moderation seemed to disappear.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Moderation retreat drove away influential cohorts, eroding X's cultural relevance and ad appeal.

insights.claim: Cultural critic Jamilah Lemieux views X's shift as a deliberate move away from the progressive Black voices that defined its earlier history and describes posting there as screaming into the void.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Perceived hostility to a core creator segment is a structural headwind for X engagement.
insights.quote: It was a very deliberate shift away from the progressive Black voices that had defined the platform for its earlier history

themes.theme: Distribution beats politics: Threads vs Bluesky/Blacksky

insights.claim: Bluesky's Blacksky custom feed and moderation service offered a safer ecosystem for Black users but has not swayed public discourse like Black Twitter's #OscarsSoWhite, partly due to platform fatigue and lack of a connected ecosystem like Meta's.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Decentralized challengers struggle without built-in distribution, favoring incumbents with existing social graphs.
insights.quote: it lacks the initial buy-in that comes from an already connected platform ecosystem like Meta’s
insights.locator: Part of that is a numbers game

insights.claim: A 2025 Pew Research Center survey found 69 percent of left-leaning news influencers who joined Bluesky did so in its first year, concentrating its base among progressives, journalists and academics.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: A narrow ideological user base limits Bluesky's mass-market ad potential.
insights.locator: In the beginning, Bluesky’s biggest user base

insights.claim: Black users care more about finding each other at volume than about a platform's overall politics, according to researcher Rianna Walcott.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Scale and discoverability, not values positioning, determine winners in social platform migrations.
insights.quote: I think it matters more to Black users where they can find each other at volume rather than the overall politics of the platform

insights.claim: Threads has more than 500 million monthly active users and, per a March Statista report, is on track to surpass X's 557 million MAU, helped by integration with Facebook and Instagram's 6 billion-plus combined users.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Threads overtaking X would mark a major shift in text-social market share toward Meta.
insights.quote: Threads has more than 500 million monthly active users

insights.claim: Meta reported in December that Threads has over 200 interest communities, such as Black Threads, Black British Threads and Black LGBTQ Threads, which make it easy for users to find niche audiences.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Community features drive engagement and retention, supporting Threads monetization.

insights.claim: Threads' cross-posting from Facebook and Instagram brings unexpected content into feeds, which users describe as Threads dropping you off anywhere.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Cross-app content seeding is a cold-start advantage competitors cannot replicate.
insights.quote: We often joke that Threads will drop you off anywhere
